newsitem.title: ISRAEL: ILO signs job creation pact with Palestinians.
newsitem.headline: ILO signs job creation pact with Palestinians.

text.p: The Palestinian Authority on Tuesday signed a $1.5 million deal with the International Labour Organisation (ILO) to develop and implement a job-creation programme in the West Bank and Gaza Strip, the ILO said.
It said that Palestinian Labour Minister Samir Ghousheh signed the agreement with ILO Assistant Director-General Shukri Dajani in Gaza in the presence of Palestinian President Yasser Arafat.

Unemployment in the West Bank and Gaza Strip, estimated to be around 50 percent, is one of the highest in the world. Thousands of Palestinians lost jobs in Israel when it closed its borders with the self-rule areas after Islamic militants killed 59 people in Israel in February and March.
The closure was gradually eased but put back in full force on October 23 for fear of Islamic Jihad attacks in revenge for the killing of the group's leader a year ago.

The Geneva-based ILO, a specialised agency of the United Nations, said money for the programme was donated by Sheikh Hamdan Bin Rashed al-Maktoum, Minister of Finance and Industry in the United Arab Emirates and deputy ruler of the emirate of Dubai.
It said the project was part of a $10.5 million ILO programme of assistance to the Palestinian people.
